## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | **Leader election** — Instances use a file lock to elect a single leader; the first instance to acquire the lock wins. If no leader is elected (lock unavailable), the instance continues operating without dispatching. | met | File-lock election: writeLockFile uses atomic O_CREAT|O_EXCL so first-to-create wins (packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts:183); non-leader instances short-circuit with no proxy polling/dispatch while continuing check-in activity (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2533), and a failed/absent lease degrades to no-dispatch (tick() leader block). |
| 2 | **Lease-based leadership** — The leader holds a 5-minute lease, refreshed every time it polls the llama-proxy. If the lease expires (leader crashed or idle), instances detect the expiry and run a new election. | met | 5-min lease DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS=300 (packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts:38); leader refreshes the lease each proxy-poll cycle via refreshLease() (leader-election.ts:299, invoked at top of every tick in downtime-worker.ts); expired-lease detection (detectStaleLeader, leader-election.ts:311) triggers cleanupStaleElection + attemptElection re-election (downtime-worker.ts leader block). |
| 3 | **Coordination file** — A shared JSON file at `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` stores one entry per instance: `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`. Each instance: | met | COORDINATION_FILE='downtime-coordination.json' written under the coordination dir = <root>/.worklog (coordination.ts:33; index.ts passes join(targetCwd,'.worklog')); CoordinationEntry shape is exactly {instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated} (coordination.ts:53-58). |
| 4 | On startup and every 30 minutes, reads the coordination file | met | DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30*60*1000 (downtime-worker.ts:209); check-in runs on the first tick because lastCheckInAt starts null ('first check-in on startup', downtime-worker.ts:2519) and then every 30 min; runCoordinationCheckIn reads the coordination file via getEntry on each check-in. |
| 5 | If it has an entry, verifies its work item is still its most important; if not, updates the entry | met | runCoordinationCheckIn re-reads the current entry, recomputes the instance's most-important item via computeMostImportantItem, and upserts a fresh entry (upsertEntry replaces the row with the new workItemId/lastUpdated) when the priority changed — downtime-worker.ts runCoordinationCheckIn (~line 1460-1510). |
| 6 | If no entry exists, adds its most important item to the list | met | With no prior entry, runCoordinationCheckIn builds a new CoordinationEntry with assignedAt = now and upsertEntry adds it under the shared coordination lock (coordination.ts upsertEntry read-modify-write; downtime-worker.ts check-in path). |
| 7 | If its entry was removed (by leader dispatch), adds a new entry on the next check-in | met | Leader removes the dispatched instance's entry (downtime-worker.ts:1606, 1622); the owner re-offers at its next 30-min check-in by recomputing its next most-important item and upserting a fresh entry (runCoordinationCheckIn cadence); the no-dead-opfer guard only removes when genuinely nothing dispatchable. |
| 8 | **Leader dispatch logic** — The leader reads the coordination file, determines priority order (audit tier first, then implement, then plan, then intake), checks LLM idle status (dispatch poll interval 10s + continuous idle threshold 60s — producer-accepted defaults, see work-item comment 2026-08-24; the 30s proxy status refresh is unchanged), and dispatches the highest-priority available item when a slot opens. The dispatched item is removed from the coordination file. | met | Leader tier order COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER = ['audit','implement','plan','intake'] (downtime-worker.ts:219), applied in dispatchFromCoordination; idle gate uses 10s poll + 60s continuous-idle defaults (DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=10_000, DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS=60_000, downtime-worker.ts:121-122); dispatched item's entry is removed (1606); docs confirm the 10s/60s producer-accepted timings (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md:98-106). |
| 9 | **Multi-worklog support** — Each instance operates on its own worklog directory (identified in the coordination file). The leader compares work items across directories using the standard tier priority system. | met | Each entry stores its own worklog root in `directory` (coordination.ts:56); the leader fetches per-directory via deps.fetchItem(entry.workItemId, entry.directory) (downtime-worker.ts:1570) and dispatches with cwd = entry.directory, comparing items across entries by the standard tier priority (classifyItemForDispatch, dispatchFromCoordination). v1 single-machine file-sharing scope is explicitly documented (leader-election.ts header) but the cross-directory comparison intent is implemented. |
